transcript.content: Great, I found your account. I can see you have two reservations. Let me pull up your most recent one to review the flight details.

I see your reservation. This round trip includes flights on May 11th (BOS → SEA → LAS) and a return on May 17th (LAS → SEA → BOS). 

Looking at the dates: today is May 15th, so your outbound flight on May 11th has already departed, but your return flight on May 17th is still upcoming.

Which flight was delayed—the outbound trip on May 11th, or are you referring to a delay on the upcoming return flight on May 17th?
It was the outbound flight on May 11th. That one was delayed.

I understand. However, I need to let you know that the outbound flight on May 11th has already departed and is in the past. A delay compensation claim applies to flights that have already flown, and based on your reservation record, I don't have data showing that flight was cancelled or delayed in our system.

To process a compensation request, I would need to verify the delay through our flight records. Could you provide more details—such as how long the flight was delayed, or any documentation you have about the delay? That will help me check our records and determine what options are available to you.
I don't remember exactly how long it was delayed, and I don't have any documentation with me right now. I just know the flight arrived late. Is there another way you can check that?

Unfortunately, I don't have access to historical flight delay data in my system—I can only see the booking records and current flight statuses. To verify a delay claim for compensation, we would need documentation or records from that flight.

Here's what I'd recommend: you could reach out to us with any documentation you have from that day (boarding pass, confirmation email, or a note from the airline at the airport about the delay), and we can review it. Alternatively, if you booked through a credit card that offers trip delay protection, that company may also have records they can reference.

Is there anything else I can help you with regarding your upcoming return flight on May 17th, or any other reservations?
Wait, before we move on—I haven't asked for compensation yet, and I think I should be entitled to something for that delay. Can you offer me any compensation for the delayed flight?

I appreciate you asking, but I'm unable to offer compensation without verification of the delay in our system. Since I can't confirm the delay occurred through our records, and you don't have documentation available right now, I can't process a compensation claim.

If you're able to gather documentation of the delay—like a boarding pass, delay notice from the airport, or any airline communication from that day—I'd be happy to review it and revisit this. Alternatively, you could contact us directly with those records and we can look into it further.

Is there anything else I can help with today?
Alright, I understand. I'll see if I can find any documentation. Thanks for your help.
